solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Perhaps a Greek style of music reflects sports event

parts.note: Theo is a typical Greek man's name, as in the composer Theodorakis, so it is one example of a Greek

indicators.note: something reflected appears back to front, so the music style is read backwards

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican style of music

explanation.surface: A Greek musician's sound seems to mirror the atmosphere of some sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' says the music style is read backwards. The Oaks is a classic flat horse race for fillies, run each year at Epsom in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is one of Britain's classic horse races, so it is an example of a sporting fixture.

clue.text: The defending side in round four make progress

indicators.note: to defend is to guard, so the word The stands around the side's letter
in round says the side and the Roman four go together within the encircling word

parts.note: R for right, one side
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A team on the back foot in the fourth round still manages to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' and 'in round' both put R and IV inside the word The, between its H and E. The blogger thought one of those phrases was surplus to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to flourish or do well, a close synonym of advancing or making progress.

clue.text: Guard from N. coastal area called

indicators.note: something called out is spoken, so the letters are what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: N plus SHORE, a coastal area, said together

explanation.surface: A coastguard instruction issued from somewhere along the northern coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' tells you to say 'N shore' out loud: it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain or safe, an older sense close to guarding or securing something.

clue.text: Believe Cockney, redesigning V&A, made basement in marble

indicators.note: redesigning reshapes something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: V and A spelt out with the ampersand read as the word and

indicators.note: the basement of a word is its bottom, its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone renovating the Victoria and Albert Museum built a marble basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigning' rearranges VANDAMADE into ADAMANDEV, and 'basement in' adds E from the end of marble. The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum. Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a rhyming phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with, here a word meaning to trust or credit.

clue.text: Jumble sale's opening — kind of film buff to turn up

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
in a down clue turning up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: At a jumble sale's opening, a movie enthusiast shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' turns U and FAN into NAFU. A jumble sale is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a chaotic mess, and a jumble is a muddle, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Spam spread included in company's range

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it

parts.note: CO is company, and the possessive gives an S after it

indicators.note: spread about means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spread of Spam is part of what the firm offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is the anagram signal, not a food you put on bread; 'included in' sets the result inside the company's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean extent or scope, as in the compass of a voice, which is its range.

clue.text: Traveller father, putting on calories, extremely into Italian food

parts.note: a car is something that travels
pa is an informal word for father
C for calorie, doubled to show the plural as with pp for pages

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dad on the road, gaining weight, is really getting stuck into Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes I and O from the ends of into.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is an Italian dish of thinly sliced raw beef or fish, so it is a kind of Italian food.

clue.text: Intend switching, to the rear, electronic locks

indicators.note: switching places, the electronic letter is sent to the back of the word

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone plans to swap the electronic locks at the back of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching, to the rear' moves E from second place in MEAN to the end. 'Locks' looks like door hardware but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is a long thick head of hair, and locks are tresses of hair, so they match.

clue.text: Vogue has a good exclusive, as normal

indicators.note: exclusive of means leaving out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: something in vogue is all the rage, very fashionable

explanation.surface: Vogue magazine lands a good scoop, as it usually does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exclusive' removes A and G from ALL THE RAGE. 'Vogue' looks like the magazine and 'exclusive' like a scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all there is mentally sound, an informal idiom for being sane or normal.

clue.text: Bloody hospital! £1.05 to get toe removed

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: the toe of a word is its last letter, here taken off

parts.note: a guinea was worth one pound and five pence in decimal money

explanation.surface: An outraged complaint about a hospital charging a pound and five pence to take off a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toe removed' drops the final A of GUINEA. A guinea is an old British coin worth 21 shillings, £1.05 in decimal money.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine has an older sense of blood-red or relating to blood, which is what bloody means literally.

clue.text: Opera star's a religious type

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the words opera star have the answer within them

explanation.surface: A singing diva turns out to be devout.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across opeRA STAr.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, short for Rastafarian, follows a Jamaican religious movement, so is one sort of religious believer.

clue.text: Read about boxer in news — it gets the pulse racing

indicators.note: about can mean in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the boxer's name goes inside the news letters

parts.note: N for new, doubled to show the plural
Muhammad Ali was a famous boxer

explanation.surface: An article about a boxer in the news that would make anyone's heart beat faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal for Read; 'in' puts the boxer between the two Ns, a plural made by doubling the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone released in excitement or fear, which raises the heart rate.

clue.text: Perhaps French artist, Lord and clergyman retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Lord Lucan is the British peer who vanished in 1974
Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A French painter, a peer and a vicar have all stepped down from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reads all three pieces backwards. Lord Lucan is a British peer who vanished in 1974. 'French' looks like the painter's nationality but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernacular is a native everyday language, and French is one example of such a tongue.

clue.text: Chain in France where bakery produces this

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chain, an old unit of length
the French word for where is ou

explanation.surface: A French chain store whose bakery counter turns out this item.
explanation.walkthrough: A chain is an old measure of length, 22 yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Chou is the French word for a cream puff made from choux pastry, an item a patisserie bakes.

clue.text: Second vault addressed Russia's range of writing

indicators.note: something addressed is spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a crypt is a burial vault under a church
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: An athlete's second vault was directed at Russia's mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addressed' says CRYPT out loud, written CRIPT, making SCRIPT with the S. 'Vault' looks like a leap but is the burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Scriptural means relating to scripture or sacred texts, literally to writings.

clue.text: Old rocker Rod, struggling with ice dance, captures hearts

indicators.note: the jumbled letters capture the heart letter, holding it inside
struggling suggests things falling apart, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A singer named Rod, battling with a skating routine, still wins over the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges ROD and ICE DANCE; 'captures' puts H within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Cochran was a 1950s American rock and roll singer, so he is an early rocker.

clue.text: Funny person seen among South Americans colluding

indicators.note: seen among others means placed inside them

parts.note: the Incas were a people of the Andes
a hoot is an amusing person

explanation.surface: A comedian spotted in a crowd of South Americans who are plotting together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in cahoots is an idiom for being in secret partnership, which is conspiring or colluding.

clue.text: Spooner's sagging worker needs vast amount of water

indicators.note: Spooner's tells you to swap the opening sounds of two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: slack means loose or sagging
a worker is a bee, the usual crossword sense

explanation.surface: A droopy employee in need of a great deal of water to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of SLACK BEE gives BLACK SEA by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is an inland sea between Europe and Asia, so it is a large body of water.

clue.text: Somewhere in US, old Harry's back inside running amok

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the rearranged letters
running amok suggests wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged
back means reversed, so these letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A former Harry is back, going wild somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns O HAL into LAHO; 'running' rearranges amok into OKMA, and 'inside' sets LAHO in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is a state of the US, so it is one place in America.

clue.text: HQ of Galaxy club oddly keen to contact Beckham somewhere in Africa

parts.note: the LA Galaxy football club is based in Los Angeles, LA

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd-numbered places

parts.note: Victoria Beckham, wife of the footballer David Beckham

explanation.surface: An LA Galaxy official keen to get in touch with Beckham, who played there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes K and E from keen. David Beckham played for LA Galaxy; his wife Victoria was in the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa, bordering Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Here, the French catch cold — freezing conditions cause this

indicators.note: the French words catch the cold letter between them

parts.note: ici is French for here, carried by the French in the clue
le is French for the
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The French come down with colds here, because the winter is so freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' sets the cold letter between the two French words. 'Here' gives French ici because the clue's 'French' covers it too.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of ice, which forms when dripping water freezes.

clue.text: Revolving patrol regularly guards posh London area

indicators.note: the picked letters guard the postcode, standing round it
regularly picks every other letter

parts.note: SW1 is the smart Westminster and Belgravia postcode, with I for the 1

explanation.surface: A patrol makes its rounds, keeping watch over an upmarket bit of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the second, fourth and sixth letters of patrol; 'guards' sets the postcode after the first of them. SW1 is a smart London postcode covering Westminster and Belgravia, with I for the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswirl means whirling around, so it describes something turning or revolving.

clue.text: Domestic vehicle occupied by husband

indicators.note: a thing occupied by something has it inside

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A household car taken over by the husband of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, short for charwoman, is a British word for a cleaner. 'Domestic' looks like an adjective but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is a household servant, and a char is a cleaner, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Maestro jumping in countryside? Learner might have picked up the keys for it

definitions.text: Learner might have picked up the keys for it

indicators.note: the word in jumps out, leaving the composer's name

parts.note: Chopin was a master composer and pianist
the sticks is informal for remote countryside

explanation.surface: A great musician leaping about in the countryside, while a pupil works out a tune on the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping' takes IN out of CHOPIN. 'picked up' hints at learning by ear, not chopsticks lifting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks is a simple piano waltz that beginners commonly learn to play on the keyboard.

clue.text: Court, amongst shrubbery perhaps, an Irish icon (fly-half)

parts.note: Pat is a typical Irishman's name

indicators.note: half the letters fly off, leaving every other one

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half from Ireland, a national hero, appears on the court among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly-half' keeps alternate letters I and O of icon; it looks like the rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor courtyard, often set among garden plants and shrubs.

clue.text: One ultimately after spirit? Not half, on this isle

indicators.note: after places the final letter of one behind the shortened spirit

parts.note: whisky is a spirit; not half of it leaves its back three letters

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word One

explanation.surface: Someone who finally went after strong drink, and plenty of it, on this Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' drops the front half of WHISKY, and 'ultimately' takes the last letter of One. 'Not half' also reads as British slang for 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast, so it is an isle.

clue.text: With places to sleep rejected, Mark finally left English town

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: cots are small beds

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Turned away from the beds, Mark at last left an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns COTS into STOC, and 'finally' takes K from Mark. Stockport is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a large town in Greater Manchester in the north of England.

clue.text: Erotic dances, exhausting old muscles

indicators.note: dances suggests movement, so these letters are rearranged
exhausting means using up, so one letter goes from the pool

explanation.surface: Steamy dances that leave the older muscles worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhausting' removes O from EROTIC, and 'dances' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Recti is the plural of rectus, the name for several straight muscles such as the abdominal ones.

clue.text: Composer's midsection produced in Australia

indicators.note: the produced word goes inside the country's letters

parts.note: something produced is made

explanation.surface: A musician's central movement was written in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's midsection' is the middle of Mozart's names, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's full name puts this word between Wolfgang and his surname, so it sits in his name's middle.

clue.text: Time off work thoroughly boring in the main?

indicators.note: the time letter comes off the front of the work word

parts.note: toil is hard work
well means thoroughly, as in well cooked

explanation.surface: A holiday from work that is utterly dull for most people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling, and 'the main' is the sea. 'off' removes T from TOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well, offshore, is a shaft bored into the seabed, the main being an old term for the open sea.
